ca_main_face.blurb: Main Face is the tall central wall on the western side of Machete Ridge in Pinnacles National Park, on the Central Coast. Fifteen routes mix aid, trad and a pair of bolted lines, running from about 5.7 up to the low 5.12s with a good share in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. Many climbs are long, multi-pitch affairs that finish on top of the ridge, and a few begin from ledges reached by an extra pitch or two. The rock is not uniformly solid, so wear a helmet and be careful about loose holds. Descents are by rappel or by walking the ridge.
ca_main_face.parking_note: Leave the car in the west side lot of the national park, which is where the trail to the wall begins.
ca_main_face.approach: From the west side lot, walk the Balconies Trail for about 0.6 miles to the junction with the Balconies Cave Trail, then follow the climbers' path marked with carabiner signs up to the base.

ca_hinterland_corridor.blurb: Hinterland Corridor is a narrow, alpine-feeling gully of splitter cracks tucked just above the Hinterland Wall in the Tahquitz and Suicide Rocks region, around 7,800 feet. Fifteen routes here are mostly trad, a few of them multi-pitch, with a single bolted line. The difficulty runs from about 5.8 to 5.11, and the bulk of the routes sit between 5.9 and 5.10. Several small buttresses and fins line the corridor, which means you can string together a day of quiet, good-quality crack climbing away from the busier faces nearby. Bring a standard trad rack.

ca_ellsmere_island.blurb: Ellsmere Island (also spelled Ellesmere) is a small cluster of crags in the North Wonderland part of Joshua Tree National Park's Wonderland of Rocks. The faces sit a short way up a hillside and carry several roofs. Routes are short but well regarded, and most of the fifteen here are trad, with a couple of top-ropes and one bolted line. Grades span easy 5.7 terrain through the 5.10s, with a few 5.11s at the top end. It is one of the closer formations to the road in this part of the park, which makes it a handy stop for a few quality pitches.

ca_big_heat_formation_the.blurb: The Big Heat Formation is a single, oddly shaped boulder at roughly 6,100 feet in the Snow Valley bouldering zone near Running Springs, in the San Bernardino Mountains. Its east side is curvy, with many corners and buttresses. Of the fifteen problems, nearly all are very easy, mostly at the VB level with a couple of V0s, which suits beginners and kids. The standout is the hard one, a V5 that has become the namesake. A slab problem is also worth a try. It lies just north of the neighbouring Voodoo Formation, a short stroll from the road.

ca_big_tower.blurb: Big Tower is a small, moderate crag in the Lower Gorge of the Owens River Gorge, near Bishop, just east of Middle Power Plant Road, around 5,000 feet up. It holds fifteen climbs, mostly bolted single-pitch sport routes with a couple of trad lines and one top-rope. Grades start at 5.5 and the heart of the crag sits in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, with a few harder lines up to 5.12. It is among the easier places in the gorge to find a gentle bolted route. The face takes sun from about mid-morning to mid-afternoon in the main season.

ca_crack_of_noon_buttress.blurb: Crack of Noon Buttress is a compact southeast-facing crag in the upper part of Pine Creek Canyon near Bishop, at around 7,000 feet. It gets excellent sun in winter. The fifteen routes are short and fun, a mix of trad and bolted lines, some of them two pitches. Most grades land between 5.8 and 5.10, but there is a handful of much harder lines, from 5.12 into the 5.13s and one 5.14. The rock is clean, high quality granodiorite, and a short walk from the road gets you there, so it works well for a quick session.
